newsitem.title: UK: British royals to get new helicopter.
newsitem.headline: British royals to get new helicopter.

text.p: Britain's royal family is to get a new helicopter in a leasing deal expected to provide significant cost savings, the Ministry of Defence said on Thursday.
The single helicopter, which will be flown by Royal Air Force pilots, will replace two ageing Wessex helicopters currently used by Queen Elizabeth and other members of the royal family.
The nearly 30-year-old Wessex helicopters have become increasingly expensive to maintain and operate, the defence ministry said.

The queen has been under pressure to save costs. Britain's new Labour government, elected on May 1, does not wish to buy her a new royal yacht at a cost of 60 million pounds, which had been promised by the outgoing Conservative administration.

The defence ministry said it would inviting private British helicopter companies to tender for the contract, whose cost will be met from a government grant provided to cover the royal family's travel costs.
The cost of the new service was not disclosed. The two existing helicopters cost up to four million pounds a year to run, with the royal household paying for the use it makes of them.
